messages:
anya: Heads-up — onboarding hf/foo-13b v1. Converted tokenizer+config with the usual hf->redwood script but getting token-count mismatches on a lot of eval prompts, and some downstream quality regressions.

sam: Can you paste a minimal repro (input + HF token counts vs converted)?

anya: Sure — small examples below. Note this is with the converter set to preserve HF normalizer by default.

anya: ```
Input: "Hello, world!"
HF tokens: 3
Converted (redwood tokenizer) tokens: 4

Input: "\u00A0NBSP at start"
HF tokens: 4
Converted tokens: 3
```

kevin: interesting. that looks like a whitespace normalization + byte-fallback combo. did the converter flip add_prefix_space or normalizer form?

anya: We set:
```json
"add_prefix_space": false,
"normalizer": "NFKC",
"byte_fallback": true
```
But HF model files had "add_prefix_space": true and normalizer was "NFC" in the original. Converter tried to preserve "byte_fallback": true but the pretokenizer step seems to run in a slightly different order, so trailing/leading spaces get absorbed.

maria: This would explain the NBSP diff — NFKC can change U+00A0 handling. Also add_prefix_space changes token boundaries for sentencepiece/byte-level tokenizers.

anya: Right. On top of that, chat template mapping expects messages to be serialized with a leading space for assistant turns (we do that for other models), but this model's HF chat template does not. So prompts that previously had a leading-space sentinel now get an extra token and break prefix caching in eval harness.

sam: Can you show the conversion config and the small patch you used? Might be a quick fix to align normalizer/order.

anya: Pasted core of converter config I used: 
```json
{
  "preserve_normalizer": true,
  "force_add_prefix_space": null,
  "map_special_tokens": {
    "bos_token": "<s>",
    "eos_token": "</s>",
    "pad_token": "<pad>"
  }
}
```

anya: But map_special_tokens ended up mapping HF "" to `` which removed an explicit pad marker in some prompt templates. Small but caused scoring diffs in reranker evals.

kevin: Oof. Two vectors then: (1) normalization differences (NFC vs NFKC) + byte fallback ordering, (2) special token mapping + add_prefix_space mismatch. Either can shift tokenization enough to change quantized kernel warm paths and KB cache hits.

maria: For the quant experiments we ran, token count drift of even 1-2 tokens triggered different batching and quant mode selection, so end-to-end latency/quality varied. We saw +3% ppl on a small dev set after conversion.

sam: Probable fixes: force normalizer to match HF (NFC), preserve add_prefix_space boolean, and ensure special token names are canonicalized (explicit pad/bos/eos). Also ensure the pretokenizer byte fallbacks run at the same phase.

anya: I tried forcing normalizer=NFC and add_prefix_space=true locally — token counts line up again on the sample set. Will run full eval.

ci-bot: conversion-job-1728501234 completed — artifacts uploaded to s3://redwood-conversions/foo-13b/v1/ (logs + tokenizer.json).

sam: Nice. After your eval, if numbers look good, add a small unit test in converter that compares HF tokenization to converted on a handful of tricky unicode+space cases (NBSP, ZWJ, leading spaces, trailing spaces).

anya: Will do. Also adding a guard: if special token is empty string, map to explicit <|pad|> for our chat templates.

maria: Thanks — can we also log when token counts differ for any eval prompt > 1 token? That made it obvious earlier.

anya: Yep — I'll send a PR with tests + a conversion flag `--align-tokenizer-phase` that forces HF ordering.

kevin: Ping me on the PR, will review for the edge cases (ZWJ + NBSP). :thumbsup:

sam: thx, team. small dramas but looks fixable.

anya: ETA for PR: today end of day.
